schema_representation.schema:
CREATE TABLE cards (

    colorIndicator TEXT -- Column Description: A list of all the colors in the color indicator (The symbol prefixed to a card's types).,
    loyalty TEXT -- Column Description: The starting loyalty value of the card., Column Value Explanation: Used only on cards with "Planeswalker" in its types. empty means unkown,
    name TEXT -- Column Description: The name of the card., Column Value Explanation: Cards with multiple faces, like "Split" and "Meld" cards are given a delimiter.,
    originalType TEXT -- Column Description: original Type, Column Value Explanation: The type of the card as originally printed. Includes any supertypes and subtypes.,
    printings TEXT -- Column Description: A list of set printing codes the card was printed in, formatted in uppercase.,
    text TEXT -- Column Description: The rules text of the card.,
    toughness TEXT -- Column Description: The toughness of the card.,
    types TEXT -- Column Description: A list of all card types of the card, including Un‑sets and gameplay variants.

);

CREATE TABLE foreign_data (

    language TEXT -- Column Description: The foreign language of card.,
    name TEXT -- Column Description: The foreign name of the card.,
    text TEXT -- Column Description: The foreign text ruling of the card.,
    uuid TEXT,
    CONSTRAINT fk_foreign_data_uuid FOREIGN KEY (uuid) REFERENCES cards (uuid)

);

CREATE TABLE legalities (

    status TEXT -- , Column Value Explanation: • legal • banned • restricted,
    uuid TEXT,
    CONSTRAINT fk_legalities_uuid FOREIGN KEY (uuid) REFERENCES cards (uuid)

);

CREATE TABLE rulings (

    id INTEGER NOT NULL -- Column Description: unique id identifying this ruling,
    text TEXT -- Column Description: description about this ruling,
    uuid TEXT,
    PRIMARY KEY (id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_rulings_uuid FOREIGN KEY (uuid) REFERENCES cards (uuid)

);

CREATE TABLE set_translations (

    language TEXT -- Column Description: language of this card set,
    setCode TEXT -- Column Description: the set code for this set,
    translation TEXT -- Column Description: translation of this card set,
    CONSTRAINT fk_set_translations_setCode FOREIGN KEY (setCode) REFERENCES sets (code)

);

CREATE TABLE sets (

    baseSetSize INTEGER -- Column Description: The number of cards in the set.,
    block TEXT -- Column Description: The block name the set was in.,
    isForeignOnly INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the set is available only outside the United States of America.,
    isOnlineOnly INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the set is only available in online game variations.,
    mcmName TEXT,
    mtgoCode TEXT -- Column Description: The set code for the set as it appears on Magic: The Gathering Online, Column Value Explanation: if the value is null or empty, then it doesn't appear on Magic: The Gathering Online,
    name TEXT -- Column Description: The name of the set.,
    tcgplayerGroupId INTEGER -- Column Description: The group identifier of the set on TCGplayer

);

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT DISTINCT T1.text FROM foreign_data AS T1 INNER JOIN cards AS T2 ON T1.uuid = T2.uuid INNER JOIN sets AS T3 ON T2.setCode = T3.code WHERE T3.name = 'Coldsnap' AND T1.language = 'Italian' AND T1.text IS NOT NULL

CREATE TABLE cards (

    id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    artist TEXT -- Column Description: The name of the artist that illustrated the card art.,
    asciiName TEXT -- Column Description: The ASCII(opens new window) (Basic/128) code formatted card name with no special unicode characters.,
    availability TEXT -- Column Description: A list of the card's available printing types., Column Value Explanation: "arena", "dreamcast", "mtgo", "paper", "shandalar",
    borderColor TEXT -- Column Description: The color of the card border., Column Value Explanation: "black", "borderless", "gold", "silver", "white",
    cardKingdomFoilId TEXT -- Column Description: card Kingdom Foil Id, Column Value Explanation: cardKingdomFoilId, when paired with cardKingdomId that is not Null, is incredibly powerful.,
    cardKingdomId TEXT -- Column Description: card Kingdom Id, Column Value Explanation: A list of all the colors in the color indicator,
    colorIdentity TEXT -- Column Description: A list of all the colors found in manaCost, colorIndicator, and text,
    colorIndicator TEXT -- Column Description: A list of all the colors in the color indicator (The symbol prefixed to a card's types).,
    colors TEXT -- Column Description: A list of all the colors in manaCost and colorIndicator., Column Value Explanation: Some cards may not have values, such as cards with "Devoid" in its text.,
    convertedManaCost REAL -- Column Description: The converted mana cost of the card. Use the manaValue property., Column Value Explanation: if value is higher, it means that this card cost more converted mana,
    duelDeck TEXT -- Column Description: The indicator for which duel deck the card is in.,
    edhrecRank INTEGER -- Column Description: The card rank on EDHRec,
    faceConvertedManaCost REAL -- Column Description: The converted mana cost or mana value for the face for either half or part of the card., Column Value Explanation: if value is higher, it means that this card cost more converted mana for the face,
    faceName TEXT -- Column Description: The name on the face of the card.,
    flavorName TEXT -- Column Description: The promotional card name printed above the true card name on special cards that has no game function., Column Value Explanation: The promotional card name printed above the true card name on special cards that has no game function.,
    flavorText TEXT -- Column Description: The italicized text found below the rules text that has no game function., Column Value Explanation: The italicized text found below the rules text that has no game function.,
    frameEffects TEXT -- Column Description: The visual frame effects., Column Value Explanation: "colorshifted", "companion", "compasslanddfc", "devoid", "draft", "etched", "extendedart", "fullart", "inverted", "legendary", "lesson", "miracle", "mooneldrazidfc", "nyxtouched", "originpwdfc", "showcase", "snow", "sunmoondfc", "textless", "tombstone", "waxingandwaningmoondfc",
    frameVersion TEXT -- Column Description: The version of the card frame style., Column Value Explanation: "1993", "1997", "2003", "2015", "future",
    hand TEXT -- Column Description: The starting maximum hand size total modifier., Column Value Explanation: A + or - character precedes an integer.   positive maximum hand size: +1, +2, .... negative maximum hand size: -1, .... neural maximum hand size: 0....,
    hasAlternativeDeckLimit INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card allows a value other than 4 copies in a deck., Column Value Explanation: 0: disallow 1: allow,
    hasContentWarning INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card marked by Wizards of the Coast (opens new window) for having sensitive content. See this official article (opens new window) for more information., Column Value Explanation: 0: doesn't have 1: has sensitve content or Wizards of the Coast  Cards with this property may have missing or degraded properties and values.,
    hasFoil INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card can be found in foil, Column Value Explanation: 0: cannot be found 1: can be found,
    hasNonFoil INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card can be found in non-foil, Column Value Explanation: 0: cannot be found 1: can be found,
    isAlternative INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card is an alternate variation to an original printing, Column Value Explanation: 0: is not 1: is,
    isFullArt INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card has full artwork., Column Value Explanation: 0: doesn't have, 1: has full artwork,
    isOnlineOnly INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card is only available in online game variations., Column Value Explanation: 0: is not 1: is,
    isOversized INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card is oversized., Column Value Explanation: 0: is not 1: is,

This means I need to retrieve the 'text' column from the 'foreign_data' table, filtered by 'language' = 'Italian'. To link these foreign data entries to the 'Coldsnap' set, I need to join 'foreign_data' with 'cards' (using 'uuid') and then with 'sets' (using a common identifier, likely 'uuid' or a related set ID). The preliminary SQL query already correctly identifies the need to join `foreign_data` with `cards` and `sets`. It also correctly filters `foreign_data.language` to 'Italian' and `sets.name` to 'Coldsnap'. The preliminary query selects `T1.text`, which corresponds to the `text` column in `foreign_data`, fulfilling the requirement for 'text ruling'. Therefore, the columns `foreign_data.text`, `foreign_data.language`, `cards.uuid`, `sets.name`, and `foreign_data.uuid` are all necessary. The `legaliites` table and its `uuid` column are not directly used in the question or the preliminary query's logic for filtering or selection, so they are not essential.

CREATE TABLE cards (

    id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    artist TEXT -- Column Description: The name of the artist that illustrated the card art.,
    asciiName TEXT -- Column Description: The ASCII(opens new window) (Basic/128) code formatted card name with no special unicode characters.,
    availability TEXT -- Column Description: A list of the card's available printing types., Column Value Explanation: "arena", "dreamcast", "mtgo", "paper", "shandalar",
    borderColor TEXT -- Column Description: The color of the card border., Column Value Explanation: "black", "borderless", "gold", "silver", "white",
    cardKingdomFoilId TEXT -- Column Description: card Kingdom Foil Id, Column Value Explanation: cardKingdomFoilId, when paired with cardKingdomId that is not Null, is incredibly powerful.,
    cardKingdomId TEXT -- Column Description: card Kingdom Id, Column Value Explanation: A list of all the colors in the color indicator,
    colorIdentity TEXT -- Column Description: A list of all the colors found in manaCost, colorIndicator, and text,
    colorIndicator TEXT -- Column Description: A list of all the colors in the color indicator (The symbol prefixed to a card's types).,
    colors TEXT -- Column Description: A list of all the colors in manaCost and colorIndicator., Column Value Explanation: Some cards may not have values, such as cards with "Devoid" in its text.,
    convertedManaCost REAL -- Column Description: The converted mana cost of the card. Use the manaValue property., Column Value Explanation: if value is higher, it means that this card cost more converted mana,
    duelDeck TEXT -- Column Description: The indicator for which duel deck the card is in.,
    edhrecRank INTEGER -- Column Description: The card rank on EDHRec,
    faceConvertedManaCost REAL -- Column Description: The converted mana cost or mana value for the face for either half or part of the card., Column Value Explanation: if value is higher, it means that this card cost more converted mana for the face,
    faceName TEXT -- Column Description: The name on the face of the card.,
    flavorName TEXT -- Column Description: The promotional card name printed above the true card name on special cards that has no game function., Column Value Explanation: The promotional card name printed above the true card name on special cards that has no game function.,
    flavorText TEXT -- Column Description: The italicized text found below the rules text that has no game function., Column Value Explanation: The italicized text found below the rules text that has no game function.,
    frameEffects TEXT -- Column Description: The visual frame effects., Column Value Explanation: "colorshifted", "companion", "compasslanddfc", "devoid", "draft", "etched", "extendedart", "fullart", "inverted", "legendary", "lesson", "miracle", "mooneldrazidfc", "nyxtouched", "originpwdfc", "showcase", "snow", "sunmoondfc", "textless", "tombstone", "waxingandwaningmoondfc",
    frameVersion TEXT -- Column Description: The version of the card frame style., Column Value Explanation: "1993", "1997", "2003", "2015", "future",
    hand TEXT -- Column Description: The starting maximum hand size total modifier., Column Value Explanation: A + or - character precedes an integer.   positive maximum hand size: +1, +2, .... negative maximum hand size: -1, .... neural maximum hand size: 0....,
    hasAlternativeDeckLimit INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card allows a value other than 4 copies in a deck., Column Value Explanation: 0: disallow 1: allow,
    hasContentWarning INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card marked by Wizards of the Coast (opens new window) for having sensitive content. See this official article (opens new window) for more information., Column Value Explanation: 0: doesn't have 1: has sensitve content or Wizards of the Coast  Cards with this property may have missing or degraded properties and values.,
    hasFoil INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card can be found in foil, Column Value Explanation: 0: cannot be found 1: can be found,
    hasNonFoil INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card can be found in non-foil, Column Value Explanation: 0: cannot be found 1: can be found,
    isAlternative INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card is an alternate variation to an original printing, Column Value Explanation: 0: is not 1: is,
    isFullArt INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card has full artwork., Column Value Explanation: 0: doesn't have, 1: has full artwork,
    isOnlineOnly INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card is only available in online game variations., Column Value Explanation: 0: is not 1: is,
    isOversized INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card is oversized., Column Value Explanation: 0: is not 1: is,

preliminary_sql:
SELECT DISTINCT
  "T2"."name"
FROM sets AS T1
INNER JOIN set_translations AS T3
  ON T1.code = T3.setCode
INNER JOIN cards AS T4
  ON T1.code = T4.setCode
INNER JOIN foreign_data AS T2
  ON T4.uuid = T2.uuid
WHERE
  T1.name = 'Coldsnap' AND T3.language = 'Italian'
ORDER BY
  "T4"."convertedManaCost" DESC
LIMIT 1;

The name column in the sets table is needed to filter for the 'Coldsnap' set. The language column in the set_translations table is needed to filter for Italian. The name column in the foreign_data table is needed to display the Italian card names. The convertedManaCost in the cards table is needed to find the card with the highest converted mana cost. The code column in the sets table and setCode column in the set_translations table are needed to join the tables. The uuid column in the cards table and foreign_data table are needed to join the tables.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT T1.name FROM foreign_data AS T1 INNER JOIN cards AS T2 ON T1.uuid = T2.uuid INNER JOIN sets AS T3 ON T2.setCode = T3.code WHERE T1.language = 'Italian' AND T3.name = 'Coldsnap' AND T2.convertedManaCost = ( SELECT MAX(T4.convertedManaCost) FROM cards AS T4 INNER JOIN sets AS T5 ON T4.setCode = T5.code WHERE T5.name = 'Coldsnap' )

schema_representation.execution_plan: Execution plan: To answer this question, I need to: 1) Find the cards in the 'Coldsnap' set, 2) Find the Italian names of these cards, 3) Find the cards with the highest convertedManaCost. The name column in the sets table is needed to filter for the 'Coldsnap' set. The language column in the set_translations table is needed to filter for Italian. The name column in the foreign_data table is needed to display the Italian card names. The convertedManaCost in the cards table is needed to find the card with the highest converted mana cost. The code column in the sets table and setCode column in the set_translations table are needed to join the tables. The uuid column in the cards table and foreign_data table are needed to join the tables.

sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT "T2"."name"
        FROM "cards" AS "T1"
        INNER JOIN "foreign_data" AS "T2"
          ON "T1"."uuid" = "T2"."uuid"
        INNER JOIN "sets" AS "T3"
          ON "T1"."setCode" = "T3"."code"
        WHERE "T3"."name" = 'Coldsnap'
          AND "T2"."language" = 'Italian'
          AND "T1"."convertedManaCost" = (
            SELECT MAX("T1_inner"."convertedManaCost")
            FROM "cards" AS "T1_inner"
            INNER JOIN "sets" AS "T3_inner"
              ON "T1_inner"."setCode" = "T3_inner"."code"
            WHERE "T3_inner"."name" = 'Coldsnap'
          );

sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT

FROM cards AS T1
INNER JOIN sets AS T2
  ON T1."setCode" = T2."code"

    WHERE
      T2_sub."name" = 'Coldsnap'
  );

selected_schemas.chain_of_thought_reasoning: The question asks for the artist of the card with the highest converted mana cost, but only for cards that do not have multiple faces. The preliminary SQL is correct, but it is missing the filter for cards without multiple faces. The side column indicates whether a card has multiple faces. Therefore, I need to filter on the side column being null. The artist column is needed to display the artist's name. The convertedManaCost column is needed to determine the highest converted mana cost. The layout column is needed to filter for normal cards.

The question asks for the illustrator of the card art with the highest converted mana cost, specifically for cards that do not have multiple faces. The 'side IS NULL' condition filters out cards with multiple faces. We need to find the maximum 'convertedManaCost' among these cards and then identify the 'artist' associated with that card. The preliminary SQL query correctly identifies the 'artist' by ordering by 'convertedManaCost' in descending order and taking the top result. Therefore, the essential columns are 'side' for filtering, 'convertedManaCost' for determining the highest cost, and 'artist' for the final output.

The 'side IS NULL' condition filters out cards with multiple faces. We need to find the maximum 'convertedManaCost' among these cards and then identify the 'artist' associated with that card. The preliminary SQL query correctly identifies the 'artist' by ordering by 'convertedManaCost' in descending order and taking the top result. Therefore, the essential columns are 'side' for filtering, 'convertedManaCost' for determining the highest cost, and 'artist' for the final output.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT "artist" FROM cards WHERE side IS NULL ORDER BY convertedManaCost DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 1

preliminary_sql:
SELECT
  T1.format
FROM legalities AS T1
INNER JOIN cards AS T2
  ON T1.uuid = T2.uuid
INNER JOIN sets AS T3
  ON T2.printings = T3.block
WHERE
  T2.originalReleaseDate = (
    SELECT
      MIN(originalReleaseDate)
    FROM cards
  )
GROUP BY
  T1.format;

selected_schemas.chain_of_thought_reasoning: The question asks for the oldest card's release date and its legal formats. The provided SQL attempts to find the minimum release date and then join to find the legal formats. The core tables involved are `cards` (for release date) and `legalities` (for legal formats). The `originalReleaseDate` column is needed to find the oldest card. The `format` column from the `legalities` table is needed to list the legal formats. The `uuid` column is needed to join the two tables.

sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT T1."originalReleaseDate", T2."format"
        FROM "cards" AS T1
        INNER JOIN "legalities" AS T2
          ON T1."uuid" = T2."uuid"
        WHERE T1."rarity" = 'mythic'
          AND T2."status" = 'Legal'
          AND T1."originalReleaseDate" = (SELECT MIN("originalReleaseDate") FROM "cards" WHERE "rarity" = 'mythic')

The provided SQL attempts to find the minimum release date and then join to find the legal formats. The core tables involved are `cards` (for release date) and `legalities` (for legal formats). The `originalReleaseDate` column is needed to find the oldest card. The `format` column from the `legalities` table is needed to list the legal formats. The `uuid` column is needed to join the two tables.

SELECT
  T1."originalReleaseDate",
  GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT T2."format") AS "legal_formats"
FROM cards AS T1
INNER JOIN legalities AS T2
  ON T1."uuid" = T2."uuid"
WHERE
  T1."originalReleaseDate" = (
    SELECT
      MIN("originalReleaseDate")
    FROM cards
  )
GROUP BY
  T1."uuid",
  T1."originalReleaseDate";

selected_schemas.chain_of_thought_reasoning: The question asks for the illustrator who illustrated the least amount of cards and the formats of play for those cards.  To answer this, I need to: 1) Find the artist who illustrated the fewest cards (using `artist` and `name` to count cards per artist). 2) Join the `cards` table with the `legalities` table using the `uuid` to link cards to their legal formats. 3) Select the `format` from the `legalities` table for the artist identified in step 1. The `artist` column is needed to identify the illustrator. The `name` column is needed to count the cards per artist. The `uuid` column is needed to join the tables. The `format` column is needed to display the format of play.

The question asks for the illustrator who illustrated the least amount of cards and the formats of play for the cards they illustrated. The preliminary SQL query correctly identifies the artist with the least number of cards by grouping by 'artist', counting 'name' (card name), ordering by this count, and taking the minimum. It then joins the 'cards' table with the 'legalities' table on 'uuid' to retrieve the 'format' for the cards illustrated by this artist. Therefore, the 'artist' column from the 'cards' table is needed to identify and filter by the illustrator. The 'uuid' column from both 'cards' and 'legalities' tables is essential for joining these two tables. The 'format' column from the 'legalities' table is required to output the formats of play. The 'name' column from the 'cards' table is used in the subquery to count the number of cards per artist.

sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT DISTINCT
  T1."artist",
  T2."format"
FROM cards AS T1
INNER JOIN legalities AS T2
  ON T1."uuid" = T2."uuid"
WHERE T1."artist" IN (
  SELECT "artist"
  FROM cards
  GROUP BY "artist"
  HAVING COUNT(*) = (
    SELECT MIN(card_count)
    FROM (
      SELECT
        COUNT(*) AS card_count
      FROM cards
      GROUP BY "artist"
    )
  )
);

schema_representation.schema:
CREATE TABLE cards (

    artist TEXT -- Column Description: The name of the artist that illustrated the card art.,
    colorIndicator TEXT -- Column Description: A list of all the colors in the color indicator (The symbol prefixed to a card's types).,
    hand TEXT -- Column Description: The starting maximum hand size total modifier., Column Value Explanation: A + or - character precedes an integer.   positive maximum hand size: +1, +2, .... negative maximum hand size: -1, .... neural maximum hand size: 0....,
    isFullArt INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card has full artwork., Column Value Explanation: 0: doesn't have, 1: has full artwork,
    layout TEXT -- Column Description: The type of card layout. For a token card, this will be "token",
    name TEXT -- Column Description: The name of the card., Column Value Explanation: Cards with multiple faces, like "Split" and "Meld" cards are given a delimiter.,
    number TEXT -- Column Description: The number of the card,
    originalType TEXT -- Column Description: original Type, Column Value Explanation: The type of the card as originally printed. Includes any supertypes and subtypes.,
    printings TEXT -- Column Description: A list of set printing codes the card was printed in, formatted in uppercase.,
    text TEXT -- Column Description: The rules text of the card.,
    toughness TEXT -- Column Description: The toughness of the card.,
    types TEXT -- Column Description: A list of all card types of the card, including Un‑sets and gameplay variants.

);

CREATE TABLE foreign_data (

    id INTEGER NOT NULL -- Column Description: unique id number identifying this row of data,
    name TEXT -- Column Description: The foreign name of the card.,
    uuid TEXT,
    PRIMARY KEY (id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_foreign_data_uuid FOREIGN KEY (uuid) REFERENCES cards (uuid)

);

CREATE TABLE legalities (

    format TEXT -- Column Description: format of play, Column Value Explanation: each value refers to different rules to play,
    uuid TEXT,
    CONSTRAINT fk_legalities_uuid FOREIGN KEY (uuid) REFERENCES cards (uuid)

);

CREATE TABLE rulings (

    uuid TEXT,
    CONSTRAINT fk_rulings_uuid FOREIGN KEY (uuid) REFERENCES cards (uuid)

);

CREATE TABLE sets (

    id INTEGER NOT NULL -- Column Description: unique id identifying this set,
    baseSetSize INTEGER -- Column Description: The number of cards in the set.,
    block TEXT -- Column Description: The block name the set was in.,
    name TEXT -- Column Description: The name of the set.,
    totalSetSize INTEGER -- Column Description: The total number of cards in the set, including promotional and related supplemental products but excluding Alchemy modifications - however those cards are included in the set itself.,
    PRIMARY KEY (id)

);

sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT DISTINCT T2."format"
FROM "cards" AS T1
INNER JOIN "legalities" AS T2
  ON T1."uuid" = T2."uuid"
WHERE T1."artist" IN (
  SELECT "artist"
  FROM "cards"
  GROUP BY "artist"
  HAVING COUNT(id) = (
    SELECT MIN(card_count)
    FROM (
      SELECT COUNT(id) AS card_count
      FROM "cards"
      GROUP BY "artist"
    )
  )
);

CREATE TABLE cards (

    id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    artist TEXT -- Column Description: The name of the artist that illustrated the card art.,
    asciiName TEXT -- Column Description: The ASCII(opens new window) (Basic/128) code formatted card name with no special unicode characters.,
    availability TEXT -- Column Description: A list of the card's available printing types., Column Value Explanation: "arena", "dreamcast", "mtgo", "paper", "shandalar",
    borderColor TEXT -- Column Description: The color of the card border., Column Value Explanation: "black", "borderless", "gold", "silver", "white",
    cardKingdomFoilId TEXT -- Column Description: card Kingdom Foil Id, Column Value Explanation: cardKingdomFoilId, when paired with cardKingdomId that is not Null, is incredibly powerful.,

    colorIdentity TEXT -- Column Description: A list of all the colors found in manaCost, colorIndicator, and text,

    colors TEXT -- Column Description: A list of all the colors in manaCost and colorIndicator., Column Value Explanation: Some cards may not have values, such as cards with "Devoid" in its text.,
    convertedManaCost REAL -- Column Description: The converted mana cost of the card. Use the manaValue property., Column Value Explanation: if value is higher, it means that this card cost more converted mana,

    edhrecRank INTEGER -- Column Description: The card rank on EDHRec,

    faceName TEXT -- Column Description: The name on the face of the card.,
    flavorName TEXT -- Column Description: The promotional card name printed above the true card name on special cards that has no game function., Column Value Explanation: The promotional card name printed above the true card name on special cards that has no game function.,
    flavorText TEXT -- Column Description: The italicized text found below the rules text that has no game function., Column Value Explanation: The italicized text found below the rules text that has no game function.,
    frameEffects TEXT -- Column Description: The visual frame effects., Column Value Explanation: "colorshifted", "companion", "compasslanddfc", "devoid", "draft", "etched", "extendedart", "fullart", "inverted", "legendary", "lesson", "miracle", "mooneldrazidfc", "nyxtouched", "originpwdfc", "showcase", "snow", "sunmoondfc", "textless", "tombstone", "waxingandwaningmoondfc",
    frameVersion TEXT -- Column Description: The version of the card frame style., Column Value Explanation: "1993", "1997", "2003", "2015", "future",
    hand TEXT -- Column Description: The starting maximum hand size total modifier., Column Value Explanation: A + or - character precedes an integer.   positive maximum hand size: +1, +2, .... negative maximum hand size: -1, .... neural maximum hand size: 0....,
    hasAlternativeDeckLimit INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card allows a value other than 4 copies in a deck., Column Value Explanation: 0: disallow 1: allow,
    hasContentWarning INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card marked by Wizards of the Coast (opens new window) for having sensitive content. See this official article (opens new window) for more information., Column Value Explanation: 0: doesn't have 1: has sensitve content or Wizards of the Coast  Cards with this property may have missing or degraded properties and values.,
    hasFoil INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card can be found in foil, Column Value Explanation: 0: cannot be found 1: can be found,
    hasNonFoil INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card can be found in non-foil, Column Value Explanation: 0: cannot be found 1: can be found,
    isAlternative INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card is an alternate variation to an original printing, Column Value Explanation: 0: is not 1: is,
    isFullArt INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card has full artwork., Column Value Explanation: 0: doesn't have, 1: has full artwork,

SELECT DISTINCT T2."format"
FROM "cards" AS T1
INNER JOIN "legalities" AS T2

The preliminary SQL query correctly identifies the artist with the least number of cards by grouping by 'artist', counting 'name' (card name), ordering by this count, and taking the minimum. It then joins the 'cards' table with the 'legalities' table on 'uuid' to retrieve the 'format' for the cards illustrated by this artist. Therefore, the 'artist' column from the 'cards' table is needed to identify and filter by the illustrator. The 'uuid' column from both 'cards' and 'legalities' tables is essential for joining these two tables. The 'format' column from the 'legalities' table is required to output the formats of play. The 'name' column from the 'cards' table is used in the subquery to count the number of cards per artist.

schema_representation.execution_plan: Execution plan: The question asks for the illustrator who illustrated the least amount of cards and the formats of play for those cards.  To answer this, I need to: 1) Find the artist who illustrated the fewest cards (using `artist` and `name` to count cards per artist). 2) Join the `cards` table with the `legalities` table using the `uuid` to link cards to their legal formats. 3) Select the `format` from the `legalities` table for the artist identified in step 1. The `artist` column is needed to identify the illustrator. The `name` column is needed to count the cards per artist. The `uuid` column is needed to join the tables. The `format` column is needed to display the format of play.

sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT DISTINCT
  T1."artist",
  T2."format"
FROM cards AS T1
INNER JOIN legalities AS T2
  ON T1."uuid" = T2."uuid"
WHERE
  T1."artist" = (
    SELECT
      "artist"
    FROM cards
    GROUP BY
      "artist"
    ORDER BY
      COUNT("uuid") ASC
    LIMIT 1
  );

schema_representation.execution_plan: Execution plan: The question asks for the illustrator who illustrated the least amount of cards and the formats of play for the cards they illustrated. The preliminary SQL query correctly identifies the artist with the least number of cards by grouping by 'artist', counting 'name' (card name), ordering by this count, and taking the minimum. It then joins the 'cards' table with the 'legalities' table on 'uuid' to retrieve the 'format' for the cards illustrated by this artist. Therefore, the 'artist' column from the 'cards' table is needed to identify and filter by the illustrator. The 'uuid' column from both 'cards' and 'legalities' tables is essential for joining these two tables. The 'format' column from the 'legalities' table is required to output the formats of play. The 'name' column from the 'cards' table is used in the subquery to count the number of cards per artist.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT DISTINCT T2.format FROM cards AS T1 INNER JOIN legalities AS T2 ON T1.uuid = T2.uuid WHERE T1.artist = (SELECT artist FROM cards GROUP BY artist ORDER BY COUNT(name) ASC LIMIT 1)

FROM "cards" AS T1
INNER JOIN "legalities" AS T2

The question asks for set names that have Korean translations but *do not* have Japanese translations. The preliminary SQL query attempts to achieve this by joining `sets` and `set_translations`. It filters for sets with Korean translations using `T2.translation LIKE '%Korean%'`. However, the subquery to exclude Japanese translations is flawed. Similarly, the subquery should check for `T2.language = 'Japanese'`. Finally, the output requires set names, which are in the `sets` table's `name` column.

    Id INTEGER NOT NULL -- Column Description: the badge id,
    UserId INTEGER -- Column Description: the unique id of the user,
    Name TEXT -- Column Description: the badge name the user obtained,
    PRIMARY KEY (Id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_badges_UserId FOREIGN KEY (UserId) REFERENCES users (Id)

);

CREATE TABLE comments (

    Id INTEGER NOT NULL -- Column Description: the comment Id,
    Score INTEGER -- Column Description: rating score, Column Value Explanation: The score is from 0 to 100. The score more than 60 refers that the comment is a positive comment. The score less than 60 refers that the comment is a negative comment.,
    UserId INTEGER -- Column Description: the id of the user who post the comment,
    UserDisplayName TEXT -- Column Description: user's display name,
    PRIMARY KEY (Id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_comments_PostId FOREIGN KEY (PostId) REFERENCES posts (Id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_comments_UserId FOREIGN KEY (UserId) REFERENCES users (Id)

);

CREATE TABLE postHistory (

    UserId INTEGER -- Column Description: the user who post the post,
    Text TEXT -- Column Description: the detailed content of the post,
    Comment TEXT -- Column Description: comments of the post,
    UserDisplayName TEXT -- Column Description: user's display name,
    CONSTRAINT fk_postHistory_PostId FOREIGN KEY (PostId) REFERENCES posts (Id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_postHistory_UserId FOREIGN KEY (UserId) REFERENCES users (Id)

);

CREATE TABLE postLinks (

    Id INTEGER NOT NULL -- Column Description: the post link id,
    PostId INTEGER -- Column Description: the post id,
    PRIMARY KEY (Id),

);

CREATE TABLE posts (

    Id INTEGER NOT NULL -- Column Description: the post id,
    Score INTEGER -- Column Description: the score of the post,
    OwnerUserId INTEGER -- Column Description: the id of the owner user,
    Title TEXT -- Column Description: the title of the post,
    Tags TEXT -- Column Description: the tag of the post,

    CONSTRAINT fk_posts_ParentId FOREIGN KEY (ParentId) REFERENCES posts (Id)

);

CREATE TABLE users (

    Reputation INTEGER -- Column Description: the user's reputation, Column Value Explanation: The user with higher reputation has more influence.,
    DisplayName TEXT -- Column Description: the user's display name,
    AboutMe TEXT -- Column Description: the self introduction of the user

    CONSTRAINT fk_votes_PostId FOREIGN KEY (PostId) REFERENCES posts (Id),

    THEN T2."PostId"
  END AS "Related_Post_Id"

schema_representation.schema:
CREATE TABLE postLinks (

    Id INTEGER NOT NULL -- Column Description: the post link id,
    CreationDate DATETIME -- Column Description: the creation date of the post link,
    PostId INTEGER -- Column Description: the post id,
    RelatedPostId INTEGER -- Column Description: the id of the related post,
    LinkTypeId INTEGER -- Column Description: the id of the link type,
    PRIMARY KEY (Id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_postLinks_PostId FOREIGN KEY (PostId) REFERENCES posts (Id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_postLinks_RelatedPostId FOREIGN KEY (RelatedPostId) REFERENCES posts (Id)

);

CREATE TABLE posts (

    Id INTEGER NOT NULL -- Column Description: the post id,
    PostTypeId INTEGER -- Column Description: the id of the post type,
    AcceptedAnswerId INTEGER -- Column Description: the accepted answer id of the post,
    CreaionDate DATETIME -- Column Description: the creation date of the post,
    Score INTEGER -- Column Description: the score of the post,
    ViewCount INTEGER -- Column Description: the view count of the post, Column Value Explanation: Higher view count means the post has higher popularity,
    Body TEXT -- Column Description: the body of the post,
    OwnerUserId INTEGER -- Column Description: the id of the owner user,
    LasActivityDate DATETIME -- Column Description: the last activity date,
    Title TEXT -- Column Description: the title of the post,
    Tags TEXT -- Column Description: the tag of the post,
    AnswerCount INTEGER -- Column Description: the total number of answers of the post,
    CommentCount INTEGER -- Column Description: the total number of comments of the post,
    FavoriteCount INTEGER -- Column Description: the total number of favorites of the post, Column Value Explanation: more favorite count refers to more valuable posts.,
    LastEditorUserId INTEGER -- Column Description: the id of the last editor,
    LastEditDate DATETIME -- Column Description: the last edit date,
    CommunityOwnedDate DATETIME -- Column Description: the community owned date,
    ParentId INTEGER -- Column Description: the id of the parent post, Column Value Explanation: If the parent id is null, the post is the root post. Otherwise, the post is the child post of other post.,
    ClosedDate DATETIME -- Column Description: the closed date of the post, Column Value Explanation: if ClosedDate is null or empty, it means this post is not well-finished if CloseDate is not null or empty, it means this post has well-finished.,
    OwnerDisplayName TEXT -- Column Description: the display name of the post owner,
    LastEditorDisplayName TEXT -- Column Description: the display name of the last editor,
    PRIMARY KEY (Id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_posts_ParentId FOREIGN KEY (ParentId) REFERENCES posts (Id)

);

CREATE TABLE badges (

    Id INTEGER NOT NULL -- Column Description: the badge id,
    UserId INTEGER -- Column Description: the unique id of the user,
    PRIMARY KEY (Id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_badges_UserId FOREIGN KEY (UserId) REFERENCES users (Id)

);

CREATE TABLE comments (

    Id INTEGER NOT NULL -- Column Description: the comment Id,
    CreationDate DATETIME -- Column Description: the creation date of the comment,
    UserId INTEGER -- Column Description: the id of the user who post the comment,
    UserDisplayName TEXT -- Column Description: user's display name,
    PRIMARY KEY (Id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_comments_PostId FOREIGN KEY (PostId) REFERENCES posts (Id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_comments_UserId FOREIGN KEY (UserId) REFERENCES users (Id)

);

CREATE TABLE postHistory (

    CreationDate DATETIME -- Column Description: the creation date of the post,
    Text TEXT -- Column Description: the detailed content of the post,
    Comment TEXT -- Column Description: comments of the post,
    UserDisplayName TEXT -- Column Description: user's display name,
    CONSTRAINT fk_postHistory_PostId FOREIGN KEY (PostId) REFERENCES posts (Id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_postHistory_UserId FOREIGN KEY (UserId) REFERENCES users (Id)

);

CREATE TABLE postLinks (

    Id INTEGER NOT NULL -- Column Description: the post link id,
    CreationDate DATETIME -- Column Description: the creation date of the post link,
    PostId INTEGER -- Column Description: the post id,
    PRIMARY KEY (Id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_postLinks_PostId FOREIGN KEY (PostId) REFERENCES posts (Id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_postLinks_RelatedPostId FOREIGN KEY (RelatedPostId) REFERENCES posts (Id)

);

CREATE TABLE posts (

    Id INTEGER NOT NULL -- Column Description: the post id,
    Tags TEXT -- Column Description: the tag of the post,
    LastEditorUserId INTEGER -- Column Description: the id of the last editor,
    ParentId INTEGER -- Column Description: the id of the parent post, Column Value Explanation: If the parent id is null, the post is the root post. Otherwise, the post is the child post of other post.,
    OwnerDisplayName TEXT -- Column Description: the display name of the post owner,
    PRIMARY KEY (Id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_posts_LastEditorUserId FOREIGN KEY (LastEditorUserId) REFERENCES users (Id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_posts_OwnerUserId FOREIGN KEY (OwnerUserId) REFERENCES users (Id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_posts_ParentId FOREIGN KEY (ParentId) REFERENCES posts (Id)

);

CREATE TABLE users (

    CreationDate DATETIME -- Column Description: the creation date of the user account,
    DisplayName TEXT -- Column Description: the user's display name

);

CREATE TABLE votes (

    CreationDate DATE -- Column Description: the creation date of the vote,
    CONSTRAINT fk_votes_PostId FOREIGN KEY (PostId) REFERENCES posts (Id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_votes_UserId FOREIGN KEY (UserId) REFERENCES users (Id)

);

    Name TEXT -- Column Description: the badge name the user obtained,
    CONSTRAINT fk_badges_UserId FOREIGN KEY (UserId) REFERENCES users (Id)

);

CREATE TABLE comments (

    PostId INTEGER -- Column Description: the unique id of the post,
    Score INTEGER -- Column Description: rating score, Column Value Explanation: The score is from 0 to 100. The score more than 60 refers that the comment is a positive comment. The score less than 60 refers that the comment is a negative comment.,
    UserDisplayName TEXT -- Column Description: user's display name,
    CONSTRAINT fk_comments_PostId FOREIGN KEY (PostId) REFERENCES posts (Id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_comments_UserId FOREIGN KEY (UserId) REFERENCES users (Id)

);

CREATE TABLE postLinks (

    PostId INTEGER -- Column Description: the post id,
    CONSTRAINT fk_postLinks_PostId FOREIGN KEY (PostId) REFERENCES posts (Id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_postLinks_RelatedPostId FOREIGN KEY (RelatedPostId) REFERENCES posts (Id)

);

CREATE TABLE posts (

    Id INTEGER NOT NULL -- Column Description: the post id,
    Score INTEGER -- Column Description: the score of the post,
    ViewCount INTEGER -- Column Description: the view count of the post, Column Value Explanation: Higher view count means the post has higher popularity,
    OwnerUserId INTEGER -- Column Description: the id of the owner user,
    Tags TEXT -- Column Description: the tag of the post,
    FavoriteCount INTEGER -- Column Description: the total number of favorites of the post, Column Value Explanation: more favorite count refers to more valuable posts.,
    ParentId INTEGER -- Column Description: the id of the parent post, Column Value Explanation: If the parent id is null, the post is the root post. Otherwise, the post is the child post of other post.,
    ClosedDate DATETIME -- Column Description: the closed date of the post, Column Value Explanation: if ClosedDate is null or empty, it means this post is not well-finished if CloseDate is not null or empty, it means this post has well-finished.,
    OwnerDisplayName TEXT -- Column Description: the display name of the post owner,
    LastEditorDisplayName TEXT -- Column Description: the display name of the last editor,
    PRIMARY KEY (Id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_posts_LastEditorUserId FOREIGN KEY (LastEditorUserId) REFERENCES users (Id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_posts_OwnerUserId FOREIGN KEY (OwnerUserId) REFERENCES users (Id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_posts_ParentId FOREIGN KEY (ParentId) REFERENCES posts (Id)

);

CREATE TABLE tags (

    Count INTEGER -- Column Description: the count of posts that contain this tag, Column Value Explanation: more counts --> this tag is more popular,
    CONSTRAINT fk_tags_ExcerptPostId FOREIGN KEY (ExcerptPostId) REFERENCES posts (Id)

);

CREATE TABLE users (

    Reputation INTEGER -- Column Description: the user's reputation, Column Value Explanation: The user with higher reputation has more influence.,
    DisplayName TEXT -- Column Description: the user's display name,
    AboutMe TEXT -- Column Description: the self introduction of the user,
    Views INTEGER -- Column Description: the number of views,
    UpVotes INTEGER -- Column Description: the number of upvotes,
    DownVotes INTEGER -- Column Description: the number of downvotes

);

CREATE TABLE votes (

    PostId INTEGER -- Column Description: the id of the post that is voted,
    CONSTRAINT fk_votes_PostId FOREIGN KEY (PostId) REFERENCES posts (Id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_votes_UserId FOREIGN KEY (UserId) REFERENCES users (Id)

);

The preliminary SQL joins users and posts, filters for child posts (ParentId is not null), orders by score descending, and limits to 1.  To correctly identify the parent's display name, we need to: 1) Find the child post with the highest score using posts.Score, 2) Get the ParentId of that post using posts.ParentId, 3) Join the posts table to itself (aliased) to get the parent post details using posts.Id = parent_post.ParentId, 4) Get the OwnerUserId of the parent post using parent_post.OwnerUserId, 5) Join users table to get the display name of the parent post's owner using users.Id = parent_post.OwnerUserId. Therefore, we need columns from the posts and users tables. The columns needed are: posts.Score (for filtering the highest score), posts.ParentId (to identify the parent post), posts.OwnerUserId (to join with users table), users.DisplayName (to display the parent post's owner's display name).

The question asks for the display name of the *parent* post for the child post with the highest score. The preliminary SQL query correctly identifies the child post with the highest score (using `WHERE "T2"."ParentId" IS NOT NULL` and `ORDER BY "T2"."Score" DESC LIMIT 1`) and returns the `DisplayName` of the *owner* of that child post. However, the question specifically asks for the display name of the *parent* post. This means we need to join `posts` with itself to link the child post's `ParentId` to the parent post's information, and then retrieve the `OwnerUserId` of the parent post and join with the `users` table to get its `DisplayName`.

The preliminary SQL joins users and posts, filters for child posts (ParentId is not null), orders by score descending, and limits to 1.  To correctly identify the parent's display name, we need to: 1) Find the child post with the highest score using posts.Score, 2) Get the ParentId of that post using posts.ParentId, 3) Join the posts table to itself (aliased) to get the parent post details using posts.Id = parent_post.ParentId, 4) Get the OwnerUserId of the parent post using parent_post.OwnerUserId, 5) Join users table to get the display name of the parent post's owner using users.Id = parent_post.OwnerUserId. Therefore, we need columns from the posts and users tables. The columns needed are: posts.Score (for filtering the highest score), posts.ParentId (to identify the parent post), posts.OwnerUserId (to join with users table), users.DisplayName (to display the parent post's owner's display name).

SELECT T2."DisplayName"
FROM "posts" AS T1
INNER JOIN "users" AS T2
  ON T1."OwnerUserId" = T2."Id"
WHERE T1."Id" = (
  SELECT "ParentId"
  FROM "posts"
  WHERE "ParentId" IS NOT NULL
  ORDER BY "Score" DESC
  LIMIT 1
);

CREATE TABLE hero_power (

    hero_id INTEGER DEFAULT NULL -- Column Description: the id of the hero Maps to superhero(id),
    power_id INTEGER DEFAULT NULL -- Column Description: the id of the power Maps to superpower(id), Column Value Explanation: In general, a superhero's attributes provide the foundation for their abilities and help to define who they are, while their powers are the specific abilities that they use to fight crime and protect others.,
    CONSTRAINT fk_hero_power_hero_id FOREIGN KEY (hero_id) REFERENCES superhero (id)

);

CREATE TABLE superhero (

    id INTEGER NOT NULL -- Column Description: the unique identifier of the superhero,
    superhero_name TEXT DEFAULT NULL -- Column Description: the name of the superhero,
    full_name TEXT DEFAULT NULL -- Column Description: the full name of the superhero, Column Value Explanation: The full name of a person typically consists of their given name, also known as their first name or personal name, and their surname, also known as their last name or family name. For example, if someone's given name is "John" and their surname is "Smith," their full name would be "John Smith.",
    gender_id INTEGER DEFAULT NULL -- Column Description: the id of the superhero's gender,
    eye_colour_id INTEGER DEFAULT NULL -- Column Description: the id of the superhero's eye color,
    hair_colour_id INTEGER DEFAULT NULL -- Column Description: the id of the superhero's hair color,
    skin_colour_id INTEGER DEFAULT NULL -- Column Description: the id of the superhero's skin color,
    race_id INTEGER DEFAULT NULL -- Column Description: the id of the superhero's race,
    publisher_id INTEGER DEFAULT NULL -- Column Description: the id of the publisher,
    alignment_id INTEGER DEFAULT NULL -- Column Description: the id of the superhero's alignment,
    height_cm INTEGER DEFAULT NULL -- Column Description: the height of the superhero, Column Value Explanation: The unit of height is centimeter. If the height_cm is NULL or 0, it means the height of the superhero is missing.,
    weight_kg INTEGER DEFAULT NULL -- Column Description: the weight of the superhero, Column Value Explanation: The unit of weight is kilogram. If the weight_kg is NULL or 0, it means the weight of the superhero is missing.,
    PRIMARY KEY (id)

);

The question asks for the eye, hair, and skin colors of female superheroes published by Dark Horse Comics. To achieve this, I need to join the `superhero` table with the `colour` table multiple times (once for eye color, once for hair color, and once for skin color) and also with the `gender` and `publisher` tables to apply the filters. The `superhero` table contains the foreign keys to these related tables. The `gender` table is needed to filter for 'Female' superheroes, and the `publisher` table is needed to filter for 'Dark Horse Comics'. The `colour` table is then joined using the respective IDs from the `superhero` table to retrieve the actual color names for eyes, hair, and skin. Therefore, the essential columns are: `superhero.eye_colour_id`, `superhero.hair_colour_id`, `superhero.skin_colour_id` to link to colors, `superhero.gender_id` and `superhero.publisher_id` for filtering, and `gender.gender` and `publisher.publisher_name` for filter values. The `colour.colour` column is needed to display the actual color names.

CREATE TABLE constructorResults (

    constructorResultsId INTEGER -- Column Description: constructor Results Id,
    raceId INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: race id,
    constructorId INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: constructor id,
    points REAL -- Column Description: points,
    status TEXT -- Column Description: status,
    PRIMARY KEY (constructorResultsId),
    CONSTRAINT fk_constructorResults_raceId FOREIGN KEY (raceId) REFERENCES races (raceId)

);

CREATE TABLE constructorStandings (

    constructorStandingsId INTEGER,
    raceId INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    constructorId INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    points REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: how many points acquired in each race,
    position INTEGER,
    positionText TEXT,
    wins INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    PRIMARY KEY (constructorStandingsId),
    CONSTRAINT fk_constructorStandings_raceId FOREIGN KEY (raceId) REFERENCES races (raceId)

);

CREATE TABLE driverStandings (

    driverStandingsId INTEGER,
    raceId INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    driverId INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    points REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    position INTEGER,
    positionText TEXT,
    wins INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: wins,
    PRIMARY KEY (driverStandingsId),
    CONSTRAINT fk_driverStandings_raceId FOREIGN KEY (raceId) REFERENCES races (raceId)

);

CREATE TABLE lapTimes (

    raceId INTEGER NOT NULL,
    driverId INTEGER NOT NULL,
    lap INTEGER NOT NULL,
    position INTEGER,
    time TEXT,
    milliseconds INTEGER,
    PRIMARY KEY (raceId, driverId, lap),
    CONSTRAINT fk_lapTimes_raceId FOREIGN KEY (raceId) REFERENCES races (raceId)

    driverId INTEGER NOT NULL,
    stop INTEGER NOT NULL,
    lap INTEGER NOT NULL,
    time TEXT NOT NULL,

CREATE TABLE qualifying (

    qualifyId INTEGER,
    raceId INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    driverId INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    constructorId INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    number INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    position INTEGER,
    q1 TEXT,
    q2 TEXT,
    q3 TEXT,
    PRIMARY KEY (qualifyId),

CREATE TABLE races (

    raceId INTEGER,
    year INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    round INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    circuitId INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    name TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    date DATE NOT NULL DEFAULT '0000-00-00',
    time TEXT,
    url TEXT,
    PRIMARY KEY (raceId)

);

CREATE TABLE results (

    resultId INTEGER -- Column Description: the unique identification number identifying race result,
    raceId INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: the identification number identifying the race,
    driverId INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    constructorId INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    number INTEGER,
    grid INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    position INTEGER,
    positionText TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    positionOrder INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    points REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    laps INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    time TEXT,
    milliseconds INTEGER,
    fastestLap INTEGER,
    rank INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    fastestLapTime TEXT,
    fastestLapSpeed TEXT,
    statusId INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    PRIMARY KEY (resultId),
    CONSTRAINT fk_results_raceId FOREIGN KEY (raceId) REFERENCES races (raceId)

);

    circuitId INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,

    date DATE NOT NULL DEFAULT '0000-00-00',
    time TEXT,
    url TEXT,
    PRIMARY KEY (raceId)

);

CREATE TABLE drivers (

    driverId INTEGER,
    driverRef TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    number INTEGER,
    code TEXT,
    forename TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    surname TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    dob DATE,
    nationality TEXT,
    url TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    PRIMARY KEY (driverId)

);

    raceId INTEGER,
    year INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    round INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    circuitId INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    name TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    date DATE NOT NULL DEFAULT '0000-00-00',
    time TEXT,
    url TEXT,
    PRIMARY KEY (raceId)

);

    resultId INTEGER -- Column Description: the unique identification number identifying race result,
    raceId INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: the identification number identifying the race,
    driverId INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    constructorId INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    number INTEGER,
    grid INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    position INTEGER,
    positionText TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    positionOrder INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    points REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    laps INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    time TEXT,
    milliseconds INTEGER,
    fastestLap INTEGER,
    rank INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    fastestLapTime TEXT,
    fastestLapSpeed TEXT,
    statusId INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    PRIMARY KEY (resultId),
    CONSTRAINT fk_results_raceId FOREIGN KEY (raceId) REFERENCES races (raceId),
    CONSTRAINT fk_results_driverId FOREIGN KEY (driverId) REFERENCES drivers (driverId)

);

sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT ( (
            (SELECT "time_milliseconds" FROM "results" WHERE "race_id" = (SELECT "race_id" FROM "races" WHERE "name" = 'Australian Grand Prix' AND "year" = 2008) AND "position" = (SELECT MAX("position") FROM "results" WHERE "race_id" = (SELECT "race_id" FROM "races" WHERE "name" = 'Australian Grand Prix' AND "year" = 2008) AND "time_milliseconds" IS NOT NULL))
            -

schema_representation.schema:
CREATE TABLE drivers (

    driverId INTEGER,
    driverRef TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    number INTEGER,
    code TEXT,
    forename TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    surname TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    dob DATE,
    nationality TEXT,
    url TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    PRIMARY KEY (driverId)

);

CREATE TABLE races (

    raceId INTEGER,
    year INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    round INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    circuitId INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    name TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    date DATE NOT NULL DEFAULT '0000-00-00',
    time TEXT,
    url TEXT,
    PRIMARY KEY (raceId)

);

CREATE TABLE results (

    resultId INTEGER -- Column Description: the unique identification number identifying race result,
    raceId INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: the identification number identifying the race,
    driverId INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    constructorId INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    number INTEGER,
    grid INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    position INTEGER,
    positionText TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    positionOrder INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    points REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    laps INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    time TEXT,
    milliseconds INTEGER,
    fastestLap INTEGER,
    rank INTEGER DEFAULT 0,
    fastestLapTime TEXT,
    fastestLapSpeed TEXT,
    statusId INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
    PRIMARY KEY (resultId),
    CONSTRAINT fk_results_raceId FOREIGN KEY (raceId) REFERENCES races (raceId),
    CONSTRAINT fk_results_driverId FOREIGN KEY (driverId) REFERENCES drivers (driverId)

);

sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT DISTINCT T1."team_long_name"
FROM "Team" AS T1
INNER JOIN "Team_Attributes" AS T2
  ON T1."team_api_id" = T2."team_api_id"
WHERE
  STRFTIME('%Y', T2."date") = '2012' AND
  (CASE T2."buildUpPlayPassingClass" WHEN 'Short' THEN 1 WHEN 'Mixed' THEN 2 WHEN 'Long' THEN 3 ELSE NULL END) > (
    SELECT AVG(CASE "buildUpPlayPassingClass" WHEN 'Short' THEN 1 WHEN 'Mixed' THEN 2 WHEN 'Long' THEN 3 ELSE NULL END)
    FROM "Team_Attributes"
    WHERE
      STRFTIME('%Y', "date") = '2012' AND
      "buildUpPlayPassingClass" IS NOT NULL
  ) AND
  (CASE T2."buildUpPlayPassingClass" WHEN 'Short' THEN 1 WHEN 'Mixed' THEN 2 WHEN 'Long' THEN 3 ELSE NULL END) IS NOT NULL;

sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT DISTINCT T1."team_long_name"
FROM Team AS T1
INNER JOIN Team_Attributes AS T2
  ON T1."id" = T2."team_api_id"
WHERE STRFTIME('%Y', T2."date") = '2012'
  AND (
    CASE T2."buildUpPlayPassingClass"
      WHEN 'Short' THEN 1
      WHEN 'Mixed' THEN 2
      WHEN 'Long' THEN 3
      ELSE NULL
    END
  ) > (
    SELECT AVG(
      CASE T3."buildUpPlayPassingClass"
        WHEN 'Short' THEN 1
        WHEN 'Mixed' THEN 2
        WHEN 'Long' THEN 3
        ELSE NULL
      END
    )
    FROM Team_Attributes AS T3
    WHERE STRFTIME('%Y', T3."date") = '2012'
  );

SELECT DISTINCT T1."team_long_name"
FROM "Team" AS T1
INNER JOIN "Team_Attributes" AS T2
  ON T1."id" = T2."team_api_id"
WHERE
  STRFTIME('%Y', T2."date") = '2012' AND T2."buildUpPlayPassing" > (
    SELECT AVG("buildUpPlayPassing")
    FROM "Team_Attributes"
    WHERE
      STRFTIME('%Y', "date") = '2012' AND "buildUpPlayPassing" IS NOT NULL
  );

sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT T1."player_name"
FROM Player AS T1
INNER JOIN Player_Attributes AS T2

WHERE

schema_representation.schema:
【DB_ID】 european_football_2
【Schema】
# Table: Country
[
(id:INTEGER, Description: the unique id for countries, Primary Key, Examples: [1, 1729, 4769, 7809, 10257]),
(name:TEXT, Description: country name, Examples: [Belgium, England, France, Germany, Italy])
]
# Table: League
[
(id:INTEGER, Description: the unique id for leagues, Primary Key, Examples: [1, 1729, 4769, 7809, 10257]),
(name:TEXT, Description: league name, Examples: [Belgium Jupiler League])
]
# Table: Match
[
(away_player_Y1:INTEGER, Examples: [1, 3]),
(goal:TEXT, Description: the goal of the match),
(shotoff:TEXT, Description: the shot off goal of the match, which is the opposite of shot on),
(cross:TEXT, Description: Balls sent into the opposition team's area from a wide position in the match)
]
# Table: Player
[
(id:INTEGER, Description: the unique id for players, Primary Key, Examples: [3879, 401, 9179, 6356, 5034]),
(player_api_id:INTEGER, Description: the id of the player api, Examples: [2625, 2752, 2768, 2770, 2790]),
(player_name:TEXT, Description: player name, Examples: [Aaron Appindangoye, Aaron Cresswell, Aaron Doran, Aaron Galindo, Aaron Hughes]),
(weight:INTEGER, Description: the player's weight, Examples: [187, 146, 163, 198, 154])
]
# Table: Player_Attributes
[
(id:INTEGER, Description: the unique id for players, Primary Key, Examples: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]),
(player_api_id:INTEGER, Description: the id of the player api, Examples: [505942, 155782, 162549, 30572, 23780]),
(preferred_foot:TEXT, Description: the player's preferred foot when attacking Value Explanation: right/ left, Examples: [right, left]),
(attacking_work_rate:TEXT, Description: the player's attacking work rate Value Explanation: commonsense reasoning:  • high: implies that the player is going to be in all of your attack moves • medium: implies that the player will select the attack actions he will join in • low: remain in his position while the team attacks, Examples: [medium, high, low, None]),
(defensive_work_rate:TEXT, Description: the player's defensive work rate Value Explanation: commonsense reasoning:  • high: remain in his position and defense while the team attacks  • medium: implies that the player will select the defensive actions he will join in • low: implies that the player is going to be in all of your attack moves instead of defensing, Examples: [medium, high, low, _0]),
(crossing:INTEGER, Description: the player's crossing score Value Explanation: commonsense reasoning:  Cross is a long pass into the opponent's goal towards the header of sixth-yard teammate.  The crossing score is between 0-100 which measures the tendency/frequency of crosses in the box.  Higher potential score means that the player performs better in crossing actions., Examples: [49, 48, 80, 79, 78]),
(volleys:INTEGER, Description: the player's volley score Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA, Examples: [44, 43, 40, 32, 29]),
(jumping:INTEGER, Description: the player's jumping score Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA, Examples: [58, 85, 84, 77, 73]),
(strength:INTEGER, Description: the player's strength score Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA, Examples: [76, 56, 50, 49, 48]),
(aggression:INTEGER, Description: the player's aggression score Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA, Examples: [71, 63, 62, 68, 67]),
(positioning:INTEGER, Description: the player's  positioning score Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA, Examples: [45, 44, 60, 58, 57]),
(marking:INTEGER, Description: the player's markingscore Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA, Examples: [65, 62, 76, 73, 72]),
(sliding_tackle:INTEGER, Description: the player's sliding tackle score Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA, Examples: [69, 66, 78, 72, 67]),
(gk_kicking:INTEGER, Description: the player's goalkeep kicking score Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA, Examples: [10, 9, 8, 45, 46])
]
# Table: Team
[
(team_long_name:TEXT, Description: the team's long name, Examples: [KRC Genk, Beerschot AC, SV Zulte-Waregem, Sporting Lokeren, KSV Cercle Brugge]),
(team_short_name:TEXT, Description: the team's short name, Examples: [GEN, BAC, ZUL, LOK, CEB])
]
# Table: Team_Attributes
[
(id:INTEGER, Description: the unique id for teams, Primary Key, Examples: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]),
(buildUpPlaySpeed:INTEGER, Description: the speed in which attacks are put together Value Explanation: the score which is between 1-00 to measure the team's attack speed, Examples: [60, 52, 47, 70, 58])
]

schema_representation.schema:
CREATE TABLE Country (

    id INTEGER -- Column Description: the unique id for countries,
    name TEXT -- Column Description: country name,
    PRIMARY KEY (id)

);

CREATE TABLE League (

    id INTEGER -- Column Description: the unique id for leagues,
    name TEXT -- Column Description: league name,
    PRIMARY KEY (id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_League_country_id FOREIGN KEY (country_id) REFERENCES country (id)

);

CREATE TABLE Match (

    away_player_Y1 INTEGER,
    goal TEXT -- Column Description: the goal of the match,
    shotoff TEXT -- Column Description: the shot off goal of the match, which is the opposite of shot on,
    cross TEXT -- Column Description: Balls sent into the opposition team's area from a wide position in the match,
    CONSTRAINT fk_Match_away_player_11 FOREIGN KEY (away_player_11) REFERENCES Player (player_api_id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_Match_away_player_10 FOREIGN KEY (away_player_10) REFERENCES Player (player_api_id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_Match_away_player_9 FOREIGN KEY (away_player_9) REFERENCES Player (player_api_id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_Match_away_player_8 FOREIGN KEY (away_player_8) REFERENCES Player (player_api_id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_Match_away_player_7 FOREIGN KEY (away_player_7) REFERENCES Player (player_api_id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_Match_away_player_6 FOREIGN KEY (away_player_6) REFERENCES Player (player_api_id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_Match_away_player_5 FOREIGN KEY (away_player_5) REFERENCES Player (player_api_id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_Match_away_player_4 FOREIGN KEY (away_player_4) REFERENCES Player (player_api_id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_Match_away_player_3 FOREIGN KEY (away_player_3) REFERENCES Player (player_api_id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_Match_away_player_2 FOREIGN KEY (away_player_2) REFERENCES Player (player_api_id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_Match_away_player_1 FOREIGN KEY (away_player_1) REFERENCES Player (player_api_id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_Match_home_player_11 FOREIGN KEY (home_player_11) REFERENCES Player (player_api_id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_Match_home_player_10 FOREIGN KEY (home_player_10) REFERENCES Player (player_api_id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_Match_home_player_9 FOREIGN KEY (home_player_9) REFERENCES Player (player_api_id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_Match_home_player_8 FOREIGN KEY (home_player_8) REFERENCES Player (player_api_id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_Match_home_player_7 FOREIGN KEY (home_player_7) REFERENCES Player (player_api_id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_Match_home_player_6 FOREIGN KEY (home_player_6) REFERENCES Player (player_api_id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_Match_home_player_5 FOREIGN KEY (home_player_5) REFERENCES Player (player_api_id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_Match_home_player_4 FOREIGN KEY (home_player_4) REFERENCES Player (player_api_id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_Match_home_player_3 FOREIGN KEY (home_player_3) REFERENCES Player (player_api_id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_Match_home_player_2 FOREIGN KEY (home_player_2) REFERENCES Player (player_api_id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_Match_home_player_1 FOREIGN KEY (home_player_1) REFERENCES Player (player_api_id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_Match_away_team_api_id FOREIGN KEY (away_team_api_id) REFERENCES Team (team_api_id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_Match_home_team_api_id FOREIGN KEY (home_team_api_id) REFERENCES Team (team_api_id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_Match_league_id FOREIGN KEY (league_id) REFERENCES League (id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_Match_country_id FOREIGN KEY (country_id) REFERENCES Country (id)

);

CREATE TABLE Player (

    id INTEGER -- Column Description: the unique id for players,
    player_api_id INTEGER -- Column Description: the id of the player api,
    player_name TEXT -- Column Description: player name,
    weight INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's weight,
    PRIMARY KEY (id)

);

CREATE TABLE Player_Attributes (

    id INTEGER -- Column Description: the unique id for players,
    player_api_id INTEGER -- Column Description: the id of the player api,
    preferred_foot TEXT -- Column Description: the player's preferred foot when attacking, Column Value Explanation: right/ left,
    attacking_work_rate TEXT -- Column Description: the player's attacking work rate, Column Value Explanation: commonsense reasoning:  • high: implies that the player is going to be in all of your attack moves • medium: implies that the player will select the attack actions he will join in • low: remain in his position while the team attacks,
    defensive_work_rate TEXT -- Column Description: the player's defensive work rate, Column Value Explanation: commonsense reasoning:  • high: remain in his position and defense while the team attacks  • medium: implies that the player will select the defensive actions he will join in • low: implies that the player is going to be in all of your attack moves instead of defensing,
    crossing INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's crossing score, Column Value Explanation: commonsense reasoning:  Cross is a long pass into the opponent's goal towards the header of sixth-yard teammate.  The crossing score is between 0-100 which measures the tendency/frequency of crosses in the box.  Higher potential score means that the player performs better in crossing actions.,
    volleys INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's volley score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    jumping INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's jumping score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    strength INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's strength score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    aggression INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's aggression score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    positioning INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's  positioning score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    marking INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's markingscore, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    sliding_tackle INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's sliding tackle score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    gk_kicking INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's goalkeep kicking score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    PRIMARY KEY (id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_Player_Attributes_player_api_id FOREIGN KEY (player_api_id) REFERENCES Player (player_api_id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_Player_Attributes_player_fifa_api_id FOREIGN KEY (player_fifa_api_id) REFERENCES Player (player_fifa_api_id)

);

CREATE TABLE Team (

    team_long_name TEXT -- Column Description: the team's long name,
    team_short_name TEXT -- Column Description: the team's short name

);

CREATE TABLE Team_Attributes (

    id INTEGER -- Column Description: the unique id for teams,
    buildUpPlaySpeed INTEGER -- Column Description: the speed in which attacks are put together, Column Value Explanation: the score which is between 1-00 to measure the team's attack speed,
    PRIMARY KEY (id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_Team_Attributes_team_api_id FOREIGN KEY (team_api_id) REFERENCES Team (team_api_id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_Team_Attributes_team_fifa_api_id FOREIGN KEY (team_fifa_api_id) REFERENCES Team (team_fifa_api_id)

);

# Table: Player
[
(id:INTEGER, Description: the unique id for players, Primary Key, Examples: [3879, 401, 9179, 6356, 5034]),
(player_api_id:INTEGER, Description: the id of the player api, Examples: [2625, 2752, 2768, 2770, 2790]),
(player_name:TEXT, Description: player name, Examples: [Aaron Appindangoye, Aaron Cresswell, Aaron Doran, Aaron Galindo, Aaron Hughes]),
(player_fifa_api_id:INTEGER, Description: the id of the player fifa api, Examples: [2, 6, 11, 16, 27]),
(birthday:TEXT, Description: the player's birthday Value Explanation: e.g. 1992-02-29 00:00:00  commonsense reasoning:  Player A is older than player B means that A's birthday is earlier than B's, Examples: [1992-02-29 00:00:00, 1989-12-15 00:00:00, 1991-05-13 00:00:00, 1982-05-08 00:00:00, 1979-11-08 00:00:00]),
(height:INTEGER, Description: the player's height, Examples: [182.88, 170.18, 172.72, 165.1, 190.5]),
(weight:INTEGER, Description: the player's weight, Examples: [187, 146, 163, 198, 154])
]
# Table: Player_Attributes
[
(id:INTEGER, Description: the unique id for players, Primary Key, Examples: [1, 2, 3, 4, 5]),
(player_fifa_api_id:INTEGER, Description: the id of the player fifa api, Examples: [218353, 189615, 186170, 140161, 17725]),
(player_api_id:INTEGER, Description: the id of the player api, Examples: [505942, 155782, 162549, 30572, 23780]),
(date:TEXT, Description: date Value Explanation: e.g. 2016-02-18 00:00:00, Examples: [2016-02-18 00:00:00, 2015-11-19 00:00:00, 2015-09-21 00:00:00, 2015-03-20 00:00:00, 2007-02-22 00:00:00]),
(overall_rating:INTEGER, Description: the overall rating of the player Value Explanation: commonsense reasoning:  The rating is between 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA.  Higher overall rating means the player has a stronger overall strength., Examples: [67, 62, 61, 74, 73]),
(potential:INTEGER, Description: potential of the player Value Explanation: commonsense reasoning:  The potential score is between 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA.  Higher potential score means that the player has more potential, Examples: [71, 66, 65, 76, 75]),
(preferred_foot:TEXT, Description: the player's preferred foot when attacking Value Explanation: right/ left, Examples: [right, left]),
(attacking_work_rate:TEXT, Description: the player's attacking work rate Value Explanation: commonsense reasoning:  • high: implies that the player is going to be in all of your attack moves • medium: implies that the player will select the attack actions he will join in • low: remain in his position while the team attacks, Examples: [medium, high, low, None]),
(defensive_work_rate:TEXT, Description: the player's defensive work rate Value Explanation: commonsense reasoning:  • high: remain in his position and defense while the team attacks  • medium: implies that the player will select the defensive actions he will join in • low: implies that the player is going to be in all of your attack moves instead of defensing, Examples: [medium, high, low, _0]),
(crossing:INTEGER, Description: the player's crossing score Value Explanation: commonsense reasoning:  Cross is a long pass into the opponent's goal towards the header of sixth-yard teammate.  The crossing score is between 0-100 which measures the tendency/frequency of crosses in the box. The 'attacking_work_rate' column in the 'Player_Attributes' table contains the information about the attacking work rate. The 'player_name' column in the 'Player' table contains the player's name.  The 'player_api_id' is needed to join the tables.
