schema_representation.schema:
CREATE TABLE Player (

    id INTEGER -- Column Description: the unique id for players,
    player_api_id INTEGER -- Column Description: the id of the player api,
    player_name TEXT -- Column Description: player name,
    player_fifa_api_id INTEGER -- Column Description: the id of the player fifa api,
    birthday TEXT -- Column Description: the player's birthday, Column Value Explanation: e.g. 1992-02-29 00:00:00  commonsense reasoning:  Player A is older than player B means that A's birthday is earlier than B's,
    height INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's height,
    weight INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's weight,
    PRIMARY KEY (id)

);

CREATE TABLE Player_Attributes (

    id INTEGER -- Column Description: the unique id for players,
    player_fifa_api_id INTEGER -- Column Description: the id of the player fifa api,
    player_api_id INTEGER -- Column Description: the id of the player api,
    date TEXT -- Column Description: date, Column Value Explanation: e.g. 2016-02-18 00:00:00,
    overall_rating INTEGER -- Column Description: the overall rating of the player, Column Value Explanation: commonsense reasoning:  The rating is between 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA.  Higher overall rating means the player has a stronger overall strength.,
    potential INTEGER -- Column Description: potential of the player, Column Value Explanation: commonsense reasoning:  The potential score is between 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA.  Higher potential score means that the player has more potential,
    preferred_foot TEXT -- Column Description: the player's preferred foot when attacking, Column Value Explanation: right/ left,
    attacking_work_rate TEXT -- Column Description: the player's attacking work rate, Column Value Explanation: commonsense reasoning:  • high: implies that the player is going to be in all of your attack moves • medium: implies that the player will select the attack actions he will join in • low: remain in his position while the team attacks,
    defensive_work_rate TEXT -- Column Description: the player's defensive work rate, Column Value Explanation: commonsense reasoning:  • high: remain in his position and defense while the team attacks  • medium: implies that the player will select the defensive actions he will join in • low: implies that the player is going to be in all of your attack moves instead of defensing,
    crossing INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's crossing score, Column Value Explanation: commonsense reasoning:  Cross is a long pass into the opponent's goal towards the header of sixth-yard teammate.  The crossing score is between 0-100 which measures the tendency/frequency of crosses in the box.  Higher potential score means that the player performs better in crossing actions.,
    finishing INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's finishing rate, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    heading_accuracy INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's heading accuracy, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    short_passing INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's short passing score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    volleys INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's volley score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    dribbling INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's dribbling score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    curve INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's curve score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    free_kick_accuracy INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's free kick accuracy, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    long_passing INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's long passing score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    ball_control INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's ball control score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    acceleration INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's acceleration score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    sprint_speed INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's sprint speed, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    agility INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's agility, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    reactions INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's reactions score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    balance INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's balance score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    shot_power INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's shot power, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    jumping INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's jumping score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    stamina INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's stamina score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    strength INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's strength score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    long_shots INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's long shots score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    aggression INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's aggression score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    interceptions INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's interceptions score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    positioning INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's  positioning score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    vision INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's vision score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    penalties INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's penalties score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    marking INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's markingscore, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    standing_tackle INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's standing tackle score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    sliding_tackle INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's sliding tackle score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    gk_diving INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's goalkeep diving score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    gk_handling INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's goalkeep diving score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    gk_kicking INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's goalkeep kicking score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    gk_positioning INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's goalkeep positioning score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    gk_reflexes INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's goalkeep reflexes score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    PRIMARY KEY (id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_Player_Attributes_player_api_id FOREIGN KEY (player_api_id) REFERENCES Player (player_api_id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_Player_Attributes_player_fifa_api_id FOREIGN KEY (player_fifa_api_id) REFERENCES Player (player_fifa_api_id)

);

【Schema】
# Table: Player
[
(player_api_id:INTEGER, Description: the id of the player api, Examples: [2625, 2752, 2768, 2770, 2790]),
(player_name:TEXT, Description: player name, Examples: [Aaron Appindangoye, Aaron Cresswell, Aaron Doran, Aaron Galindo, Aaron Hughes])
]
# Table: Player_Attributes
[
(player_api_id:INTEGER, Description: the id of the player api, Examples: [505942, 155782, 162549, 30572, 23780]),
(attacking_work_rate:TEXT, Description: the player's attacking work rate Value Explanation: commonsense reasoning:  • high: implies that the player is going to be in all of your attack moves • medium: implies that the player will select the attack actions he will join in • low: remain in his position while the team attacks, Examples: [medium, high, low, None])
]
【Foreign keys】
Player_Attributes.player_api_id=Player.player_api_id
Player_Attributes.player_fifa_api_id=Player.player_fifa_api_id

The 'player_api_id' is needed to join the tables.

schema_representation.execution_plan: Execution plan: The question asks to identify players who tend to be attacking when their teammates are attacking. The hint and the 'RELEVANT ENTITIES' section both point to `Player_Attributes.attacking_work_rate = 'high'` as the condition for this behavior. The preliminary SQL query correctly identifies the need to join `Player` and `Player_Attributes` tables and filter by `attacking_work_rate = 'high'`. The question specifically asks for the player's name, which is available in the `Player` table. Therefore, `Player.player_name` is needed for the output, and `Player_Attributes.attacking_work_rate` is needed for filtering.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT DISTINCT T1."player_name" FROM Player AS T1 INNER JOIN Player_Attributes AS T2 ON T1."player_api_id" = T2."player_api_id" WHERE T2."attacking_work_rate" = 'high'

CREATE TABLE Player (

    id INTEGER -- Column Description: the unique id for players,
    player_api_id INTEGER -- Column Description: the id of the player api,
    player_name TEXT -- Column Description: player name,
    player_fifa_api_id INTEGER -- Column Description: the id of the player fifa api,
    birthday TEXT -- Column Description: the player's birthday, Column Value Explanation: e.g. 1992-02-29 00:00:00  commonsense reasoning:  Player A is older than player B means that A's birthday is earlier than B's,
    height INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's height,
    weight INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's weight,
    PRIMARY KEY (id)

);

CREATE TABLE Player_Attributes (

    id INTEGER -- Column Description: the unique id for players,
    player_fifa_api_id INTEGER -- Column Description: the id of the player fifa api,
    player_api_id INTEGER -- Column Description: the id of the player api,
    date TEXT -- Column Description: date, Column Value Explanation: e.g. 2016-02-18 00:00:00,
    overall_rating INTEGER -- Column Description: the overall rating of the player, Column Value Explanation: commonsense reasoning:  The rating is between 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA.  Higher overall rating means the player has a stronger overall strength.,
    potential INTEGER -- Column Description: potential of the player, Column Value Explanation: commonsense reasoning:  The potential score is between 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA.  Higher potential score means that the player has more potential,
    preferred_foot TEXT -- Column Description: the player's preferred foot when attacking, Column Value Explanation: right/ left,
    attacking_work_rate TEXT -- Column Description: the player's attacking work rate, Column Value Explanation: commonsense reasoning:  • high: implies that the player is going to be in all of your attack moves • medium: implies that the player will select the attack actions he will join in • low: remain in his position while the team attacks,
    defensive_work_rate TEXT -- Column Description: the player's defensive work rate, Column Value Explanation: commonsense reasoning:  • high: remain in his position and defense while the team attacks  • medium: implies that the player will select the defensive actions he will join in • low: implies that the player is going to be in all of your attack moves instead of defensing,
    crossing INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's crossing score, Column Value Explanation: commonsense reasoning:  Cross is a long pass into the opponent's goal towards the header of sixth-yard teammate.  The crossing score is between 0-100 which measures the tendency/frequency of crosses in the box.  Higher potential score means that the player performs better in crossing actions.,
    finishing INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's finishing rate, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    heading_accuracy INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's heading accuracy, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    short_passing INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's short passing score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    volleys INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's volley score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    dribbling INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's dribbling score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    curve INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's curve score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    free_kick_accuracy INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's free kick accuracy, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    long_passing INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's long passing score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    ball_control INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's ball control score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    acceleration INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's acceleration score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    sprint_speed INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's sprint speed, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    agility INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's agility, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    reactions INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's reactions score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    balance INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's balance score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    shot_power INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's shot power, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    jumping INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's jumping score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    stamina INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's stamina score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    strength INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's strength score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    long_shots INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's long shots score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    aggression INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's aggression score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    interceptions INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's interceptions score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    positioning INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's  positioning score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    vision INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's vision score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    penalties INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's penalties score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    marking INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's markingscore, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    standing_tackle INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's standing tackle score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    sliding_tackle INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's sliding tackle score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    gk_diving INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's goalkeep diving score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    gk_handling INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's goalkeep diving score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    gk_kicking INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's goalkeep kicking score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    gk_positioning INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's goalkeep positioning score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    gk_reflexes INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's goalkeep reflexes score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    PRIMARY KEY (id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_Player_Attributes_player_api_id FOREIGN KEY (player_api_id) REFERENCES Player (player_api_id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_Player_Attributes_player_fifa_api_id FOREIGN KEY (player_fifa_api_id) REFERENCES Player (player_fifa_api_id)

);

The preliminary SQL query correctly identifies the need to join `Player` and `Player_Attributes` tables and filter by `attacking_work_rate = 'high'`. 【Schema】
# Table: Player
[
(player_name:TEXT, Description: player name, Examples: [Aaron Appindangoye, Aaron Cresswell, Aaron Doran, Aaron Galindo, Aaron Hughes])
]
# Table: Player_Attributes
[
(attacking_work_rate:TEXT, Description: the player's attacking work rate Value Explanation: commonsense reasoning:  • high: implies that the player is going to be in all of your attack moves • medium: implies that the player will select the attack actions he will join in • low: remain in his position while the team attacks, Examples: [medium, high, low, None])
]
【Foreign keys】
Player_Attributes.player_api_id=Player.player_api_id
Player_Attributes.player_fifa_api_id=Player.player_fifa_api_id
schema_representation.execution_plan: Execution plan: The question asks to identify players who tend to be attacking when their teammates are attacking. The hint and the 'RELEVANT ENTITIES' section both point to `Player_Attributes.attacking_work_rate = 'high'` as the condition for this behavior. The preliminary SQL query correctly identifies the need to join `Player` and `Player_Attributes` tables and filter by `attacking_work_rate = 'high'`. The question specifically asks for the player's name, which is available in the `Player` table. Therefore, `Player.player_name` is needed for the output, and `Player_Attributes.attacking_work_rate` is needed for filtering.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT DISTINCT T1."player_name" FROM Player AS T1 INNER JOIN Player_Attributes AS T2 ON T1."player_api_id" = T2."player_api_id" WHERE T2."attacking_work_rate" = 'high'

sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT
  T1."ID",
  CASE
    WHEN T2."ALP" < 300
    THEN 'Yes'
    ELSE 'No'
  END AS "ALP_within_normal_range"
FROM Patient AS T1
INNER JOIN (
  SELECT
    "ID",
    "ALP",
    "Date",
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY "ID" ORDER BY "Date" DESC) AS rn
  FROM Laboratory
) AS T2
  ON T1."ID" = T2."ID"
WHERE
  T1."Birthday" = '1982-04-01' AND T2.rn = 1;

WITH Patient1982 AS (
  SELECT
    "ID"
  FROM Patient
  WHERE
    STRFTIME('%Y', "Birthday") = '1982'
), LatestLab AS (
  SELECT
    L."ID",
    L."ALB",
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (
      PARTITION BY
        L."ID"
      ORDER BY
        L."Date" DESC
    ) AS rn
  FROM Laboratory AS L
  INNER JOIN Patient1982 AS P
    ON L."ID" = P."ID"
)
SELECT
  "ID",
  CASE
    WHEN "ALB" > 3.5 AND "ALB" < 5.5
    THEN 'Normal'
    ELSE 'Not Normal'
  END AS "Albumin Status"
FROM LatestLab
WHERE
  rn = 1;

CREATE TABLE Examination (

    ID INTEGER -- Column Description: identification of the patient,
    ANA INTEGER -- Column Description: anti-nucleus antibody concentration,
    KCT TEXT -- Column Description: measure of degree of coagulation, Column Value Explanation: +: positive  -: negative,
    CONSTRAINT fk_Examination_ID FOREIGN KEY (ID) REFERENCES Patient (ID)

);

CREATE TABLE Laboratory (

    ID INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: identification of the patient,
    Date DATE NOT NULL DEFAULT '0000-00-00' -- Column Description: Date of the laboratory tests (YYMMDD),
    GPT INTEGER -- Column Description: ALT glutamic pyruvic transaminase, Column Value Explanation: Commonsense evidence:  Normal range: N < 60,
    ALP INTEGER -- Column Description: alkaliphophatase, Column Value Explanation: Commonsense evidence:  Normal range: N < 300,
    CRE REAL -- Column Description: creatinine, Column Value Explanation: Commonsense evidence:  Normal range: N < 1.5,
    T-BIL REAL -- Column Description: total bilirubin, Column Value Explanation: Commonsense evidence:  Normal range: N < 2.0,
    T-CHO INTEGER -- Column Description: total cholesterol, Column Value Explanation: Commonsense evidence: Normal range: N < 250,
    TG INTEGER -- Column Description: triglyceride, Column Value Explanation: Commonsense evidence:  Normal range: N < 200,
    HGB REAL -- Column Description: Hemoglobin, Column Value Explanation: Commonsense evidence:  Normal range: 10 < N < 17,
    PLT INTEGER -- Column Description: platelet, Column Value Explanation: Commonsense evidence:  Normal range: 100 < N < 400,
    PT REAL -- Column Description: prothrombin time, Column Value Explanation: Commonsense evidence:  Normal range: N < 14,
    FG REAL -- Column Description: fibrinogen, Column Value Explanation: Commonsense evidence:  Normal range: 150 < N < 450,
    TAT INTEGER,
    C3 INTEGER -- Column Description: complement 3, Column Value Explanation: Commonsense evidence:  Normal range: N > 35,
    SC170 TEXT -- Column Description: anti-scl70, Column Value Explanation: Commonsense evidence:  Normal range: N= -, +-,
    SSB TEXT -- Column Description: anti-SSB, Column Value Explanation: Commonsense evidence:  Normal range: N= -, +-,
    PRIMARY KEY (ID, Date),
    CONSTRAINT fk_Laboratory_ID FOREIGN KEY (ID) REFERENCES Patient (ID)

);

CREATE TABLE Patient (

    ID INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: identification of the patient,
    SEX TEXT -- Column Description: Sex, Column Value Explanation: F: female; M: male,
    Birthday DATE -- Column Description: Birthday,
    Description DATE -- Column Description: the first date when a patient data was recorded, Column Value Explanation: null or empty: not recorded,
    First Date DATE -- Column Description: the date when a patient came to the hospital,
    Admission TEXT -- Column Description: patient was admitted to the hospital (+) or followed at the outpatient clinic (-), Column Value Explanation: patient was admitted to the hospital (+) or followed at the outpatient clinic (-),
    PRIMARY KEY (ID)

);

    ID INTEGER -- Column Description: identification of the patient,
    ANA INTEGER -- Column Description: anti-nucleus antibody concentration,
    LAC TEXT -- Column Description: measure of degree of coagulation, Column Value Explanation: +: positive  -: negative,
    CONSTRAINT fk_Examination_ID FOREIGN KEY (ID) REFERENCES Patient (ID)

);

CREATE TABLE Laboratory (

    ID INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: identification of the patient,
    Date DATE NOT NULL DEFAULT '0000-00-00' -- Column Description: Date of the laboratory tests (YYMMDD),
    GPT INTEGER -- Column Description: ALT glutamic pyruvic transaminase, Column Value Explanation: Commonsense evidence:  Normal range: N < 60,
    LDH INTEGER -- Column Description: lactate dehydrogenase, Column Value Explanation: Commonsense evidence:  Normal range: N < 500,
    RBC REAL -- Column Description: Red blood cell, Column Value Explanation: Commonsense evidence:  Normal range: 3.5 < N < 6.0,
    PT REAL -- Column Description: prothrombin time, Column Value Explanation: Commonsense evidence:  Normal range: N < 14,
    FG REAL -- Column Description: fibrinogen, Column Value Explanation: Commonsense evidence:  Normal range: 150 < N < 450,
    TAT INTEGER,
    U-PRO TEXT -- Column Description: proteinuria, Column Value Explanation: Commonsense evidence:  Normal range: 0 < N < 30,
    CRP TEXT -- Column Description: C-reactive protein, Column Value Explanation: Commonsense evidence:  Normal range: N= -, +-, or N < 1.0,
    RA TEXT -- Column Description: Rhuematoid Factor, Column Value Explanation: Commonsense evidence:  Normal range: N= -, +-,
    RF TEXT -- Column Description: RAHA, Column Value Explanation: Commonsense evidence:  Normal range: N < 20,
    C3 INTEGER -- Column Description: complement 3, Column Value Explanation: Commonsense evidence:  Normal range: N > 35,
    RNP TEXT -- Column Description: anti-ribonuclear protein, Column Value Explanation: Commonsense evidence:  Normal range: N= -, +-,
    SSB TEXT -- Column Description: anti-SSB, Column Value Explanation: Commonsense evidence:  Normal range: N= -, +-,
    PRIMARY KEY (ID, Date),
    CONSTRAINT fk_Laboratory_ID FOREIGN KEY (ID) REFERENCES Patient (ID)

);

CREATE TABLE Patient (

    ID INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: identification of the patient,
    SEX TEXT -- Column Description: Sex, Column Value Explanation: F: female; M: male,
    Birthday DATE -- Column Description: Birthday,
    First Date DATE -- Column Description: the date when a patient came to the hospital,
    Admission TEXT -- Column Description: patient was admitted to the hospital (+) or followed at the outpatient clinic (-), Column Value Explanation: patient was admitted to the hospital (+) or followed at the outpatient clinic (-),
    PRIMARY KEY (ID)

);

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT T1.Birthday FROM Patient AS T1 INNER JOIN Laboratory AS T2 ON T1.ID = T2.ID WHERE T2.RNP NOT IN ('-', '+-') ORDER BY T1.Birthday DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 1

    category TEXT -- Column Description: The area for which the amount is budgeted, such as, advertisement, food, parking,
    spent REAL -- Column Description: The total amount spent in the budgeted category for an event., Column Value Explanation: the unit is dollar. This is summarized from the Expense table,
    remaining REAL -- Column Description: A value calculated as the amount budgeted minus the amount spent, Column Value Explanation: the unit is dollar   If the remaining < 0, it means that the cost has exceeded the budget.,
    amount INTEGER -- Column Description: The amount budgeted for the specified category and event, Column Value Explanation: the unit is dollar   some computation like: amount = spent + remaining,
    event_status TEXT -- Column Description: the status of the event, Column Value Explanation: Closed / Open/ Planning    • Closed: It means that the event is closed. The spent and the remaining won't change anymore. • Open: It means that the event is already opened. The spent and the remaining will change with new expenses. • Planning: The event is not started yet but is planning. The spent and the remaining won't change at this stage.,
    link_to_event TEXT -- Column Description: The unique identifier of the event to which the budget line applies., Column Value Explanation: References the Event table,
    PRIMARY KEY (budget_id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_budget_link_to_event FOREIGN KEY (link_to_event) REFERENCES event (event_id)

);

CREATE TABLE event (

    event_id TEXT -- Column Description: A unique identifier for the event,
    event_name TEXT -- Column Description: event name,
    event_date TEXT -- Column Description: The date the event took place or is scheduled to take place, Column Value Explanation: e.g. 2020-03-10T12:00:00,
    type TEXT -- Column Description: The kind of event, such as game, social, election,
    PRIMARY KEY (event_id)

);

CREATE TABLE expense (

    expense_id TEXT -- Column Description: unique id of income,
    cost REAL -- Column Description: The dollar amount of the expense, Column Value Explanation: the unit is dollar,
    link_to_member TEXT -- Column Description: The member who incurred the expense,
    link_to_budget TEXT -- Column Description: The unique identifier of the record in the Budget table that indicates the expected total expenditure for a given category and event., Column Value Explanation: References the Budget table,
    PRIMARY KEY (expense_id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_expense_link_to_budget FOREIGN KEY (link_to_budget) REFERENCES budget (budget_id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_expense_link_to_member FOREIGN KEY (link_to_member) REFERENCES member (member_id)

);

CREATE TABLE income (

    amount INTEGER -- Column Description: amount of funds, Column Value Explanation: the unit is dollar,
    CONSTRAINT fk_income_link_to_member FOREIGN KEY (link_to_member) REFERENCES member (member_id)

);

CREATE TABLE member (

    member_id TEXT -- Column Description: unique id of member,
    position TEXT -- Column Description: The position the member holds in the club,
    link_to_major TEXT -- Column Description: The unique identifier of the major of the member. References the Major table,
    PRIMARY KEY (member_id)

);

schema_representation.schema:
CREATE TABLE budget (

    budget_id TEXT -- Column Description: A unique identifier for the budget entry,
    spent REAL -- Column Description: The total amount spent in the budgeted category for an event., Column Value Explanation: the unit is dollar. This is summarized from the Expense table,
    remaining REAL -- Column Description: A value calculated as the amount budgeted minus the amount spent, Column Value Explanation: the unit is dollar   If the remaining < 0, it means that the cost has exceeded the budget.,
    amount INTEGER -- Column Description: The amount budgeted for the specified category and event, Column Value Explanation: the unit is dollar   some computation like: amount = spent + remaining,
    event_status TEXT -- Column Description: the status of the event, Column Value Explanation: Closed / Open/ Planning    • Closed: It means that the event is closed. The spent and the remaining won't change anymore. • Open: It means that the event is already opened. The spent and the remaining will change with new expenses. • Planning: The event is not started yet but is planning. The spent and the remaining won't change at this stage.,
    link_to_event TEXT -- Column Description: The unique identifier of the event to which the budget line applies., Column Value Explanation: References the Event table,
    PRIMARY KEY (budget_id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_budget_link_to_event FOREIGN KEY (link_to_event) REFERENCES event (event_id)

);

CREATE TABLE event (

    event_id TEXT -- Column Description: A unique identifier for the event,
    event_name TEXT -- Column Description: event name,
    event_date TEXT -- Column Description: The date the event took place or is scheduled to take place, Column Value Explanation: e.g. 2020-03-10T12:00:00,
    type TEXT -- Column Description: The kind of event, such as game, social, election,
    location TEXT -- Column Description: Address where the event was held or is to be held or the name of such a location,
    status TEXT -- Column Description: One of three values indicating if the event is in planning, is opened, or is closed, Column Value Explanation: Open/ Closed/ Planning,
    PRIMARY KEY (event_id)

);

CREATE TABLE expense (

    expense_id TEXT -- Column Description: unique id of income,
    cost REAL -- Column Description: The dollar amount of the expense, Column Value Explanation: the unit is dollar,
    link_to_member TEXT -- Column Description: The member who incurred the expense,
    link_to_budget TEXT -- Column Description: The unique identifier of the record in the Budget table that indicates the expected total expenditure for a given category and event., Column Value Explanation: References the Budget table,
    PRIMARY KEY (expense_id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_expense_link_to_budget FOREIGN KEY (link_to_budget) REFERENCES budget (budget_id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_expense_link_to_member FOREIGN KEY (link_to_member) REFERENCES member (member_id)

);

CREATE TABLE income (

    source TEXT -- Column Description: A value indicating where the funds come from such as dues, or the annual university allocation,
    CONSTRAINT fk_income_link_to_member FOREIGN KEY (link_to_member) REFERENCES member (member_id)

);

CREATE TABLE major (

    major_name TEXT -- Column Description: major name,
    college TEXT -- Column Description: The name college that houses the department that offers the major

);

CREATE TABLE member (

    member_id TEXT -- Column Description: unique id of member,
    first_name TEXT -- Column Description: member's first name,
    last_name TEXT -- Column Description: member's last name, Column Value Explanation: full name is first_name + last_name. e.g. A member's first name is Angela and last name is Sanders. Thus, his/her full name is Angela Sanders.,
    position TEXT -- Column Description: The position the member holds in the club,
    link_to_major TEXT -- Column Description: The unique identifier of the major of the member. References the Major table,
    PRIMARY KEY (member_id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_member_link_to_major FOREIGN KEY (link_to_major) REFERENCES major (major_id)

);

We need to filter for parking expenses and calculate the average parking cost. Then, we compare each event's parking cost to this average.  The `event` table provides the event names (though the schema doesn't have an event_name, we can use event_id as the question is asking for the name of the event). The `budget` table links events to budget categories (parking). The `expense` table contains the actual costs.  The `category` column in `budget` is used to filter for 'Parking'. The `cost` column in `expense` is used to calculate the average parking cost and compare against the cost of each event. The `link_to_event` in `budget` and `event_id` in `event` are needed for joining the tables. The `link_to_budget` in `expense` and `budget_id` in `budget` are needed for joining the tables.

SELECT DISTINCT
  T1."event_name"
FROM event AS T1
INNER JOIN budget AS T2
  ON T1."event_id" = T2."link_to_event"
INNER JOIN expense AS T3
  ON T2."budget_id" = T3."link_to_budget"
WHERE
  T2."category" = 'Parking'
GROUP BY
  T1."event_id",
  T1."event_name"
HAVING
  SUM(T3."cost") < (
    SELECT
      AVG(EventParkingCosts."total_parking_cost")
    FROM (
      SELECT
        SUM(T6."cost") AS "total_parking_cost"
      FROM event AS T4
      INNER JOIN budget AS T5
        ON T4."event_id" = T5."link_to_event"
      INNER JOIN expense AS T6
        ON T5."budget_id" = T6."link_to_budget"
      WHERE
        T5."category" = 'Parking'
      GROUP BY
        T4."event_id"
    ) AS EventParkingCosts
  );

The spent and the remaining won't change anymore. • Open: It means that the event is already opened. The spent and the remaining will change with new expenses. • Planning: The event is not started yet but is planning. The spent and the remaining won't change at this stage.,
    link_to_event TEXT -- Column Description: The unique identifier of the event to which the budget line applies., Column Value Explanation: References the Event table,
    PRIMARY KEY (budget_id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_budget_link_to_event FOREIGN KEY (link_to_event) REFERENCES event (event_id)

    status TEXT -- Column Description: One of three values indicating if the event is in planning, is opened, or is closed, Column Value Explanation: Open/ Closed/ Planning,
    PRIMARY KEY (event_id)

);

CREATE TABLE budget (

    category TEXT -- Column Description: The area for which the amount is budgeted, such as, advertisement, food, parking,
    spent REAL -- Column Description: The total amount spent in the budgeted category for an event., Column Value Explanation: the unit is dollar. This is summarized from the Expense table,
    remaining REAL -- Column Description: A value calculated as the amount budgeted minus the amount spent, Column Value Explanation: the unit is dollar   If the remaining < 0, it means that the cost has exceeded the budget.,
    amount INTEGER -- Column Description: The amount budgeted for the specified category and event, Column Value Explanation: the unit is dollar   some computation like: amount = spent + remaining,
    event_status TEXT -- Column Description: the status of the event, Column Value Explanation: Closed / Open/ Planning    • Closed: It means that the event is closed. The spent and the remaining won't change anymore. • Open: It means that the event is already opened. The spent and the remaining will change with new expenses. • Planning: The event is not started yet but is planning. The spent and the remaining won't change at this stage.,
    link_to_event TEXT -- Column Description: The unique identifier of the event to which the budget line applies., Column Value Explanation: References the Event table,
    CONSTRAINT fk_budget_link_to_event FOREIGN KEY (link_to_event) REFERENCES event (event_id)

);

CREATE TABLE event (

    event_id TEXT -- Column Description: A unique identifier for the event,
    event_date TEXT -- Column Description: The date the event took place or is scheduled to take place, Column Value Explanation: e.g. 2020-03-10T12:00:00,
    type TEXT -- Column Description: The kind of event, such as game, social, election,
    PRIMARY KEY (event_id)

);

CREATE TABLE expense (

    expense_id TEXT -- Column Description: unique id of income,
    expense_description TEXT -- Column Description: A textual description of what the money was spend for,
    cost REAL -- Column Description: The dollar amount of the expense, Column Value Explanation: the unit is dollar,
    approved TEXT -- Column Description: A true or false value indicating if the expense was approved, Column Value Explanation: true/ false,
    link_to_member TEXT -- Column Description: The member who incurred the expense,
    link_to_budget TEXT -- Column Description: The unique identifier of the record in the Budget table that indicates the expected total expenditure for a given category and event., Column Value Explanation: References the Budget table,
    PRIMARY KEY (expense_id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_expense_link_to_budget FOREIGN KEY (link_to_budget) REFERENCES budget (budget_id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_expense_link_to_member FOREIGN KEY (link_to_member) REFERENCES member (member_id)

);

CREATE TABLE income (

    date_received TEXT -- Column Description: the date that the fund received,
    amount INTEGER -- Column Description: amount of funds, Column Value Explanation: the unit is dollar,
    CONSTRAINT fk_income_link_to_member FOREIGN KEY (link_to_member) REFERENCES member (member_id)

);

CREATE TABLE member (

    member_id TEXT -- Column Description: unique id of member,
    email TEXT -- Column Description: member's email,
    link_to_major TEXT -- Column Description: The unique identifier of the major of the member. References the Major table,
    PRIMARY KEY (member_id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_member_zip FOREIGN KEY (zip) REFERENCES zip_code (zip_code)

);

CREATE TABLE zip_code (

    type TEXT -- Column Description: The kind of ZIP code, Column Value Explanation: � Standard: the normal codes with which most people are familiar  � PO Box: zip codes have post office boxes  � Unique: zip codes that are assigned to individual organizations.

);

schema_representation.schema:
CREATE TABLE budget (

    budget_id TEXT -- Column Description: A unique identifier for the budget entry,
    category TEXT -- Column Description: The area for which the amount is budgeted, such as, advertisement, food, parking,
    spent REAL -- Column Description: The total amount spent in the budgeted category for an event., Column Value Explanation: the unit is dollar. This is summarized from the Expense table,
    remaining REAL -- Column Description: A value calculated as the amount budgeted minus the amount spent, Column Value Explanation: the unit is dollar   If the remaining < 0, it means that the cost has exceeded the budget.,
    amount INTEGER -- Column Description: The amount budgeted for the specified category and event, Column Value Explanation: the unit is dollar   some computation like: amount = spent + remaining,
    event_status TEXT -- Column Description: the status of the event, Column Value Explanation: Closed / Open/ Planning    • Closed: It means that the event is closed. The spent and the remaining won't change anymore. • Open: It means that the event is already opened. The spent and the remaining will change with new expenses. • Planning: The event is not started yet but is planning. The spent and the remaining won't change at this stage.,
    link_to_event TEXT -- Column Description: The unique identifier of the event to which the budget line applies., Column Value Explanation: References the Event table,
    PRIMARY KEY (budget_id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_budget_link_to_event FOREIGN KEY (link_to_event) REFERENCES event (event_id)

);

CREATE TABLE event (

    event_id TEXT -- Column Description: A unique identifier for the event,
    event_name TEXT -- Column Description: event name,
    event_date TEXT -- Column Description: The date the event took place or is scheduled to take place, Column Value Explanation: e.g. 2020-03-10T12:00:00,
    type TEXT -- Column Description: The kind of event, such as game, social, election,
    notes TEXT -- Column Description: A free text field for any notes about the event,
    location TEXT -- Column Description: Address where the event was held or is to be held or the name of such a location,
    status TEXT -- Column Description: One of three values indicating if the event is in planning, is opened, or is closed, Column Value Explanation: Open/ Closed/ Planning,
    PRIMARY KEY (event_id)

);

user_query: For all the people who paid more than 29.00 per unit of product id No.5. Give their consumption status in the August of 2012.

phrases: Price per unit of product = Price / Amount

Description.column_description: Description

preliminary_sql:
SELECT DISTINCT
  "T1"."Consumption"
FROM yearmonth AS T1
INNER JOIN transactions_1k AS T2
  ON T1."CustomerID" = T2."CustomerID"
WHERE
  T2."ProductID" = 5 AND T2."Price" / T2."Amount" > 29.00 AND T1."Date" LIKE '201208';

FROM yearmonth AS T2

    SELECT DISTINCT T1."CustomerID"
    FROM transactions_1k AS T1

WHERE SUBSTR(T2."Date", 1, 6) = '201208';
